Subject: Debrief: Aisha Khan (Data Scientist) — score clarifications & closure

Team —

Thanks for joining the loop earlier. Aisha finished the onsite pair of interviews (system design + infra deep dive + product case) this morning. We have partial scorecards in Greenhouse but some sections are blank or marked "uncertain" — specifically around product judgment and system-scalability tradeoffs.

Quick asks:
- Can each of you drop a one-paragraph justification for any score you gave 3 or below (so we can capture concerns for hiring committee)?
- If you have a blocking objection, mark it explicitly ("BLOCKING: reason").
- Final vote (Yes / No / Hold) by 11:00 AM PT today — we want to either close or send a short follow-up.

I attached the raw scorecard and my short notes; I also started a shared doc (link below) to capture consolidated rationale. I'll synthesize once votes are in.

Attachments: Aisha_Khan_scorecard.pdf (stub) — please add inline comments in the shared doc if you disagree with wording.

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Debrief: Aisha Khan (Data Scientist) — score clarifications & closure

On Fri, Jun 18, 2027 at 9:14 AM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Thanks for joining the loop earlier...
>
Thanks — quick notes and my votes below. I included one-line callouts for anything I flagged.

My scores (scale 1-5):
- Technical (algorithms / model analysis): 4 — good intuition on gradient-flow tradeoffs, solid code clarity.
- System design (scalable inference): 3 — proposed a batching + KV-cache approach but left out cache invalidation on model rollouts (questionable).
- Product judgment: 3 — focused on latency-first tradeoffs; missed a user-cost constraint in the scenario.

Justifications / flags:
- SYSTEM DESIGN: Proposed distributed KV cache sharding that looked feasible but didn't address migration during model version rollback. That is something our infra team will need to own; not a showstopper but risks operational burden.
- PRODUCT: Her answers prioritized p99 latency without quantifying cost impact; for a mid-market customer we might need a different balance.

Vote: HOLD — I'd like a short follow-up with a senior infra engineer to probe rollout/migration plan.

Priyom
Staff ML Engineer
priom_das@redwood.com

Adding my quick take.

- Technical depth: 4
- System design: 4
- Product judgment: 3

Vote: YES, with the caveat that we document migration/runbook expectations in the offer (or follow-up sweeper call).

Thanks both — consolidated summary below and next step.

Aggregate (mean) scores by area:
- Technical depth: 4.0
- System design: 3.5
- Product judgment: 3.0

Votes: Laura = YES; Priyom = HOLD; Camila (rec) = YES (lean hire)

Rationale: Strong modeling skillset and pragmatic design thinking; main risk is operational burden on rollout/migration and a minor behavioral flag (documented). Priyom's hold is reasonable — I support a short 20-minute follow-up with an infra engineer to walk through rollback strategies. This is a targeted probe, not a full re-interview.

Action items / timeline:
- Priyom: if you can identify a 20-minute slot before EOD, I'll schedule a short call with Aisha + one infra engineer (Laura volunteered as backup). If no slot today, we move forward with an offer that includes a written runbook request before start.
- Recruiting: please prepare a draft offer framework (title range, start window, and the runbook as a post-offer condition); cc'd recruiting@redwood.com.
- I'll synthesize the final write-up and upload the consolidated scorecard (attached) to the candidate record.

Attachments: consolidated_scorecard_Aisha_Khan.pdf (stub) — also: interview-notes-20270618.docx (stub)
